Require Import LibExtra AbstractSyntax TypingMode GeneralTyping.

Require Import OperationalSemantics ConfigTyping MethodCall.

Theorem SefG_I :
  forall (typing_mode : Mode) (w1 : var) (m : met_label) (w2 : var)
         (TZv : typ) (c1 : config) (G : ctx) (c4 : config) (k : nat),
  mode_has_sef typing_mode ->
  mode_has_mutability typing_mode ->
  config_trm c1 = trm_call (avar_f w1) m (avar_f w2) ->
  (G ⁏ (config_env c1) ⊢ w1 ∶ typ_rcd (dec_met m typ_nocap TZv typ_top) /\
   G ⁏ (config_env c1) ⊢ w2 ∶ TZv /\
   G ⁏ (config_env c1) ⊢ typ_nocap <: TZv) ->
  (exists T1, ty_config G c1 T1) ->

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import AbstractSyntax OperationalSemantics.

Inductive method_call_begin: config -> Prop :=
| method_call_begin_c w1 m w2 fs S e Lv:
  method_call_begin (trm_call (avar_f w1) m (avar_f w2); fs; S; e; Lv).

Definition config_stack C := (
  match C with
  t1 ; fs1 ; S1 ; e1 ; Lv1 => fs1
  end
).

Definition config_trm C := (
  match C with
  t1 ; fs1 ; S1 ; e1 ; Lv1 => t1
  end
).

Definition frame_within C1 m := (
  forall k C4,
    k <= m ->
    C1 ⊣ k ↦* C4 ->
    stack_suffix (config_stack C1) (config_stack C4)
).

Definition frame_end_in C1 m C3 := (
  C1 ⊣ m ↦* C3 /\
  frame_within C1 m /\
  (config_stack C3) = (config_stack C1) /\
  exists w3,
    (config_trm C3) = (trm_var (avar_f w3))
).

Definition frame_end_in' C1 m C3 := (
  C1 ⊣ m ↦* C3 /\
  (config_stack C3) = (config_stack C1) /\
  exists w3,
    (config_trm C3) = (trm_var (avar_f w3))
).

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Inductive mode :=
  | basic
  | basic_no_fun
  | basic_incap
  | basic_sef_typing
  | rodot
  | rodot_top_nm
  | rodot_nm_compl
  | rodot_nm_muttop
  | rodot_nm_compl_muttop
  | rodot_sef.

Class Mode := mode_m: mode.

Definition mode_has_fun' m: bool := match m with
| basic | basic_sef_typing => true
| _ => false
end.

Notation mode_has_fun m := ((mode_has_fun' m) = true)(only parsing).

Definition mode_has_mutability' m: bool := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => true
| _ => false
end.

Notation mode_has_mutability m := ((mode_has_mutability' m) = true)(only parsing).

Inductive mode_visibility := mode_visibility_all | mode_visibility_hide_method.

Definition mode_visibility' m: mode_visibility := match m with
| rodot | rodot_top_nm | rodot_nm_compl | rodot_nm_muttop | rodot_nm_compl_muttop | rodot_sef => mode_visibility_hide_method

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Deref HeapUpdate.

Reserved Notation "t1 ↦ t2" (at level 40, t2 at level 39).

Inductive red : config -> config -> Prop :=

| red_read : forall yObj wObj m Sigma e Lv yVal wVal ds fs,
    fresh_in_config (wVal :: nil) (trm_read (avar_f wObj) m; fs ; Sigma; e; Lv) ->
    binds wObj yObj e ->
    binds yObj (item_obj ds) Sigma ->
    defs_has ds (def_fld m (avar_f yVal)) ->
    (trm_read (avar_f wObj) m; fs ; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (trm_var (avar_f wVal); fs; Sigma; e & wVal ~ yVal; fv_config (trm_read (avar_f wObj) m; fs ; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_write : forall yObj wObj m Sigma e Lv yArg wArg Sigma' fs,
    heap_update Sigma yObj m yArg Sigma' ->
    binds wObj yObj e ->
    binds wArg yArg e ->
    (trm_write (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (trm_var (avar_f wArg); fs ; Sigma'; e; fv_config (trm_write (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_call : forall yObj wObj m Sigma e Lv wArg t ds fs,
    binds yObj (item_obj ds) Sigma ->
    defs_has ds (def_met m t) ->
    binds wObj yObj e ->
    (trm_call (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs ; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ ((open wArg (open_rec 1 wObj t)); fs ; Sigma; e; fv_config (trm_call (avar_f wObj) m (avar_f wArg); fs ; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_apply : forall yFun wFun wArg Sigma e Lv t fs,
    binds yFun (item_fun t) Sigma ->
    binds wFun yFun e ->
    (trm_apply (avar_f wFun) (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open wArg t; fs; Sigma; e; fv_config (trm_apply (avar_f wFun) (avar_f wArg); fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_fun : forall T t1 t2 Sigma e Lv y w fs,
    fresh_in_config (y :: w :: nil) (trm_lit (lit_fun T t1) t2 ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv) ->
    y <> w ->
    (trm_lit (lit_fun T t1) t2 ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open w t2 ; fs; Sigma & y ~ (item_fun t1); e & w ~ y ; fv_config (trm_lit (lit_fun T t1) t2 ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_obj : forall T ds t Sigma e Lv y w fs,
    fresh_in_config (y :: w :: nil) (trm_lit (lit_obj T ds) t ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv) ->
    w <> y ->
    (trm_lit (lit_obj T ds) t ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open w t ; fs; Sigma & y ~ (item_obj (deref_defs (e & w ~ y) (open w ds))); e & w ~ y ; fv_config (trm_lit (lit_obj T ds) t ; fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_var : forall t Sigma e Lv x fs,
    (trm_var (avar_f x); (stack_cons (frame_let t) fs); Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (open x t; fs; Sigma; e ; fv_config (trm_var (avar_f x); (stack_cons (frame_let t) fs); Sigma; e; Lv))

| red_let_push : forall s t fs Sigma e Lv,
    (trm_let s t; fs; Sigma; e; Lv)
      ↦ (s; (stack_cons (frame_let t) fs); Sigma; e ; fv_config (trm_let s t; fs; Sigma; e; Lv))

where "t1 ↦ t2" := (red t1 t2).

Inductive answer: config -> Prop :=
| nf_loc: forall x Sigma e Lv, answer (trm_var (avar_f x); stack_nil; Sigma; e; Lv).

Reserved Notation "C1 ⊣ n ↦* C2"
         (at level 40, n at level 41, C2 at level 39).

Inductive red_closure :  config -> nat -> config -> Prop :=

| red_refl : forall (C : config),
    C ⊣ 0 ↦* C

| red_trans : forall (C1 C2 C3 : config) (n : nat),
    C1 ⊣ n ↦* C2 ->
    C2      ↦  C3 ->
    C1 ⊣ S n ↦* C3

where "C1 ⊣ n ↦* C2" := (red_closure C1 n C2).

Definition config_terminates_in C n :=
 (exists (Ca : config), answer Ca /\ (C ⊣n↦* Ca)).

Definition config_terminates C :=
 (exists (n : nat), config_terminates_in C n).

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import AbstractSyntax TypingMode GeneralTyping RecordTypes InertContext TFree TFreeTyping HeapCorrespondence ConfigVarkinds NothingFresh ConfigNotations.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Inductive ty_stack : ctx -> renv -> typ -> stack -> typ -> Prop :=
  | ty_stack_nil : forall G e T U,
      G⁏e ⊢ T <: U ->
      ty_stack G e T stack_nil U
  | ty_stack_let : forall L G e s t S T U,
      ty_stack G e T s U ->
      (forall x,
          x \notin L ->
          G § x / v_let ~ S ⁏e ⊢ open x t ∶ T) ->
      ty_stack G e S (stack_cons (frame_let t) s) U.

Inductive heap_closed: heap -> Prop :=
| heap_closed_empty: heap_closed empty
| heap_closed_push S x i:
    heap_closed S ->
    closed i ->
    heap_closed (S & x ~ i)
.

Inductive config_closed: config -> Prop:=
  config_sealed_cfg t s Sigma e Lv:
    closed t ->
    closed s ->
    heap_closed Sigma ->
    config_closed (t; s; Sigma; e; Lv).

Inductive ty_config : ctx -> config -> typ -> Prop :=
| ty_config_c : forall G e s Sigma Lv t T U,
    inert G ->
    heap_correspond G e Sigma ->
    ty_stack G e T s U ->
    all_tfree_k_stack G s v_ref ->
    G⁏e ⊢ t ∶ T ->
    all_tfree_k G t v_ref ->
    ty_nothing_fresh_in_config G U (t ; s ; Sigma ; e; Lv) ->
    has_null Lv ->
    sealed G ->
    config_closed (t; s; Sigma; e; Lv) ->
    closed U ->
    ty_config G (t; s; Sigma; e; Lv) U.

Inductive config_typd : config -> typ -> Prop :=
| config_typd_c : forall Gamma c U,
    ty_config Gamma c U ->
    config_typd c U.

Inductive config_hastyp : config -> Prop :=
| config_hastyp_c : forall Gamma c U,
    ty_config Gamma c U ->
    config_hastyp c.

Notation "'⊢' c '∶' T" := (config_typd c T) (at level 40, c at level 59).

Notation config_initial_mk_typ t T null := (t; stack_nil; empty; empty; \{ null } \u fv t \u fv T) (only parsing).

Inductive config_initial: trm -> config -> Prop :=
  config_initial_mk t Lv: config_initial t (t; stack_nil; empty; empty; Lv).

End WithTypingMode.

Notation "'⊢' c '∶' T" := (config_typd _ c T) (at level 40, c at level 59).

Arguments ty_config {typing_mode}.

Arguments ty_stack {typing_mode}.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

End WithTypingMode.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import Coq.Bool.Bool.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import Vars TransformCollect Types Terms Envs.

Inductive item : Set :=
  | item_obj: defs -> item
  | item_fun: trm -> item.

Definition fv_item (v: item) : vars :=
  match v with
  | item_obj ds => (fv ds)
  | item_fun t => (fv t)
  end.

Instance ItemFreeVar : FreeVar item := fv_item.

Definition open_rec_item (n: nat) (x: var) (v: item) : item :=
  match v with
  | item_obj ds => item_obj (open_rec n x ds)
  | item_fun t => item_fun (open_rec (S n) x t)
  end.

Instance ItemOpenable : Openable item := open_rec_item.

Definition subst_item x y (v: item) : item :=
  match v with
  | item_obj ds => item_obj (subst_var x y ds)
  | item_fun t => item_fun (subst_var x y t)
  end.

Instance ItemSubstVar : SubstVar item := subst_item.

Instance ItemAbstractSyntax :
  AbstractSyntax ItemOpenable ItemFreeVar ItemSubstVar := {}.

Definition seal_rec_item (n: nat) (x: var) (v: item) : item :=
  match v with
  | item_obj ds => item_obj (seal_rec n x ds)
  | item_fun t => item_fun (seal_rec (S n) x t)
  end.

Instance ItemSealable : Sealable item := seal_rec_item.

Definition collect_item {C: Type} (df : C) (f : avar -> C) (comb: C -> C -> C) (it: item) : C :=
  match it with
  | item_obj ds => (collect df f comb ds)
  | item_fun t => (collect df f comb t)
  end.

Instance ItemCollect : Collect AvarAbstractSyntax ItemAbstractSyntax :=
  @collect_item.

Definition transform_item (f : avar -> nat -> avar) (it : item) (n : nat) : item :=
  match it with
  | item_obj ds => (item_obj (transform f ds n))
  | item_fun t => (item_fun (transform f t (S n)))
  end.

Instance ItemTransform : Transform AvarAbstractSyntax ItemAbstractSyntax :=
  @transform_item.

Notation heap := (env item).

Notation fv_heap Sigma := ((@dom item Sigma) \u (fv_env Sigma)).

Definition subst_heap x y : heap -> heap := map (subst_var x y).

Notation subheap_unchanged S1 S2 :=
  (forall y itm, binds y itm S1 -> binds y itm S2) (only parsing).

Class Fields (A: Type) :=
  fields: A -> vars.

Definition fields_def d: vars :=
  match d with
    | def_typ A T => \{}
    | def_met a t => \{}
    | def_fld a (avar_f x) => \{x}
    | def_fld a (avar_b n) => \{}
  end.

Instance FieldsDef: Fields def := fields_def.

Fixpoint fields_defs ds: vars :=
  match ds with
    | defs_nil => \{}
    | defs_cons ds d => (fields_defs ds) \u (fields d)
  end.

Instance FieldsDefs: Fields defs := fields_defs.

Fixpoint fields_item it: vars :=
  match it with
    | item_fun f => \{}
    | item_obj ds => (fields ds)
  end.

Instance FieldsItem: Fields item := fields_item.

Fixpoint fields_heap (S: heap) : vars :=
  match S with
    | nil%list => \{}
    | ((y,ds)::E)%list => (fields_heap E) \u (fields ds)
  end.

Instance FieldsHeap: Fields heap := fields_heap.

Class FieldsInFv (A: Set) {AF: Fields A}{AV: FreeVar A} :=
  fields_in_fv (a: A): fields a \c fv a.

503	  and11 G e T U: ST G e (typ_and T U) T;
504	  and12 G e T U: ST G e (typ_and T U) U;
505	  and2 G e S T U:
506	    ST G e S T ->
507	    ST G e S U ->
508	    ST G e S (typ_and T U);
509	  or11 G e T U: ST G e T (typ_or T U);
510	  or12 G e T U: ST G e U (typ_or T U);
511	  or2 G e S T U:
512	    ST G e S T ->
513	    ST G e U T ->
514	    ST G e (typ_or S U) T;
515	  trans G e S T U:
516	    ST G e S T ->
517	    ST G e T U ->
518	    ST G e S U;
519	}.
520

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra AbstractSyntax.

Require Import Equivalence Indep.

Require Export TypingMode TypingContext.

Notation EnvProperty A B := (forall (e:renv) (v: A) (T: B), Prop).

Notation TypingProperty A B := (forall (G:ctx) (Go: objctx) (e:renv) (v: A) (T: B), Prop).

Class DecTyping (A : Set) := obj_dec_typing: ctx -> objctx -> renv -> A -> dec -> Prop.

Notation "G '§§' Go '⁏' e ⊢ t '∶d' T" := (obj_dec_typing G Go e t T) (at level 40, Go at level 39, e at level 39, t at level 59).

Class Typing (A : Set) := obj_typing: ctx -> objctx -> renv -> A -> typ -> Prop.

Notation "G '§§' Go '⁏' e ⊢ t '∶' T" := (obj_typing G Go e t T) (at level 40, Go at level 39, e at level 39, t at level 59).

Notation typing G e a t := (obj_typing G objctx_empty e a t).

Notation "G '⁏' e ⊢ t '∶' T" := (typing G e t T) (at level 40, e at level 39, t at level 59).

Notation dec_typing G e a d := (obj_dec_typing G objctx_empty e a d).

Notation "G '⁏' e ⊢ t '∶d' T" := (dec_typing G e t T) (at level 40, e at level 39, t at level 59).

Class Subtyping := subtyping: ctx -> objctx -> renv -> typ -> typ -> Prop.

Notation "G '⁏' e '⊢' T '<:' U" := (subtyping G objctx_empty e T U) (at level 40, e at level 39, T at level 59).

Class ReferenceIncapacitate := obj_ref_incap :
                                 ctx -> objctx -> renv -> typ -> typ -> Prop.

Notation "G '§§' Go '⁏' e  ⊢ T1 '∶icp' T2" := (obj_ref_incap G Go e T1 T2)
  (at level 40, Go at level 39, e at level 39, T1 at level 59, T2 at level 59).

Notation ref_incap G e T1 T2 := (obj_ref_incap G objctx_empty e T1 T2).

Notation "G '⁏' e ⊢ T1 '∶icp' T2" :=
  (ref_incap G e T1 T2)
    (at level 40, e at level 39, T1 at level 59, T2 at level 59).

Class CapabilityBound (C : typ_refcap_label) :=
  obj_cap_bnd :
     ctx -> objctx -> renv -> typ -> typ -> Prop.

Notation "G '§§' Go '⁏' e  ⊢ T1 '∶cpb' ⟦ C ⟧  T2" := (@obj_cap_bnd C _ G Go e T1 T2)
  (at level 40, Go at level 39, e at level 39, T1 at level 59, T2 at level 59).

Notation cap_bnd C G e T1 T2 := (@obj_cap_bnd C _ G objctx_empty e T1 T2).

Notation "G '⁏' e ⊢ T1 '∶cpb' ⟦ C ⟧ T2" := (cap_bnd C G e T1 T2)
    (at level 40, e at level 39, T1 at level 59, T2 at level 59).

Notation typ_cap_adapt C x Tcap := (
  typ_cap_marker C (typ_or Tcap
    (typ_sel (avar_f x) (typ_label_refcap C) (avar_b 0))
  )).

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Inductive ty_var : Typing var :=

| ty_var_var : forall G e x T,
    ctx_binds x T G ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ T

| ty_rec_intro : forall G e x T,
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ open x T ->
    typ_indep_b 0 T ->

    ((mode_has_incap typing_mode) -> (G⁏e ⊢ (open x T) ∶icp (open x T))) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_bnd T

| ty_rec_elim : forall G e x T,
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_bnd T ->
    typ_indep_b 0 T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ open x T

| ty_var_and : forall G e x T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ U ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_and T U

| ty_var_sub : forall G e x T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T <: U ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ U

| ty_var_mut_top : forall G e x T,
    mode_has_mutability typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ (typ_mut_marker typ_top)

with subtyp : Subtyping :=

| subtyp_top: forall G e T,
    G⁏e ⊢ T <: typ_top

| subtyp_bot: forall G e T,
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_bot <: T

| subtyp_refl: forall G e T,
    G⁏e ⊢ T <: T

| subtyp_trans: forall G e S T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ S <: T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T <: U ->
    G⁏e ⊢ S <: U

| subtyp_and11: forall G e T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_and T U <: T

| subtyp_and12: forall G e T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_and T U <: U

| subtyp_and2: forall G e S T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ S <: T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ S <: U ->
    G⁏e ⊢ S <: typ_and T U

| subtyp_or11: forall G e T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ T <: typ_or T U

| subtyp_or12: forall G e T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ U <: typ_or T U

| subtyp_or2: forall G e S T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ S <: T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ U <: T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_or S U <: T

| subtyp_fld: forall G e a T1 T2 U1 U2,
    G⁏e ⊢ T1 <: T2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ U1 <: U2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_fld a T2 U1) <: typ_rcd (dec_fld a T1 U2)

| subtyp_typ: forall G e A S1 T1 S2 T2,
    (forall x, G⁏e ⊢ (open x S2) <: (open x S1)) ->
    (forall x, G⁏e ⊢ (open x T1) <: (open x T2)) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_typ A S1 T1) <: typ_rcd (dec_typ A S2 T2)

| subtyp_sel2: forall G e x A y S T,
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ (open y S) <: typ_sel (avar_f x) A (avar_f y)

| subtyp_sel1: forall G e x A y S T,
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_typ A S T) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_sel (avar_f x) A (avar_f y) <: (open y T)

| subtyp_fun: forall L G e S1 T1 S2 T2,
    mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ S2 <: S1 ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
       G § x / v_par ~ S2 ⁏e ⊢ open x T1 <: open x T2) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_fun S1 T1 <: typ_fun S2 T2

| subtyp_met: forall L G e m TC1 TZ1 TR1 TC2 TZ2 TR2,
    G⁏e ⊢ TZ2 <: TZ1 ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
    G § x / v_par ~ TZ2 ⁏e ⊢ open x TC2 <: open x TC1) ->

    (mode_has_sef typing_mode -> typ_indep_b 0 TC2 -> typ_indep_b 0 TC1) ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
     forall y, y <> x -> y \notin L ->
    (ctx_met G x TZ2 y TC2) ⁏e ⊢ open_met x y TR1 <: open_met x y TR2) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_met m TC1 TZ1 TR1) <: typ_rcd (dec_met m TC2 TZ2 TR2)

| subtyp_tyq: forall G e T1 T2,
    e ⊢ T1 ≈ T2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T1 <: T2

| subtyp_typ_and: forall G e A S1 T1 S2 T2,
    G⁏e ⊢
     typ_and
       (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S1 T1))
       (typ_rcd (dec_typ A S2 T2))
     <: typ_rcd (dec_typ A (typ_or S1 S2) (typ_and T1 T2))

| subtyp_dist: forall G e T1 T2 T3,
    G⁏e ⊢
      typ_and T1 (typ_or T2 T3)
      <: typ_or (typ_and T1 T2) (typ_and T1 T3)

| subtyp_nocap_bnd G e T:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_nocap <: typ_bnd T

| subtyp_nocap_typ G e A T1 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_nocap <: typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) T1 T2)

| subtyp_nocap_fld G e a T1 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_nocap <: typ_rcd (dec_fld a T1 T2)

| subtyp_nocap_met G e a TC TZ TR:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_nocap <: typ_rcd (dec_met a TC TZ TR)

| subtyp_nocap_fun G e TZ TR:
    mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_nocap <: typ_fun TZ TR

| subtyp_nocap_mut_top_boundless G e T1 T2:
    mode_has_top_nm_subtype_boundless typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_top <: (typ_or typ_nocap (typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap typ_refcap_mutability) T1 T2)))

| subtyp_nocap_mut_top_complement G e:
    mode_has_top_nm_complement typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_top <: (typ_or typ_nocap (typ_mut_marker typ_bot) )

| subtyp_nocap_mut_bot G e:
    mode_has_top_nm_complement typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ (typ_and typ_nocap (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)) <: typ_bot

| subtyp_mut_top G e:
    mode_has_mut_top typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_top <: (typ_mut_marker typ_top)

with ty_incap : ReferenceIncapacitate :=

| ty_incap_top G e:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_top ∶icp typ_top

| ty_incap_bot G e:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_bot ∶icp typ_nocap

| ty_incap_typ G e A S T:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) S T)
     ∶icp typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) S T)

| ty_incap_cap G e M S T:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap M) S T)
     ∶icp typ_top

| ty_incap_met G e m TC TZ TR:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_met m TC TZ TR) ∶icp typ_rcd (dec_met m TC TZ TR)

| ty_incap_fld G e a T1 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_fld a T1 T2) ∶icp typ_rcd (dec_fld a T1 T2)

| ty_incap_sel G e x B y S T T':
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_typ B S T) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ (open y T) ∶icp T' ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_sel (avar_f x) B (avar_f y) ∶icp T'

| ty_incap_rec G e T:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_bnd T ∶icp typ_bnd T

| ty_incap_and G e S1 T1 S2 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ S1 ∶icp S2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T1 ∶icp T2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_and S1 T1 ∶icp typ_and S2 T2

| ty_incap_or G e S1 T1 S2 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ S1 ∶icp S2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T1 ∶icp T2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_or S1 T1 ∶icp typ_or S2 T2

| ty_incap_fun G e S T:
    mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_fun S T ∶icp typ_fun S T

| ty_incap_nocap G e T:
    mode_incap' typing_mode = mode_incap_nocap ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_nocap <: T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T ∶icp T
.

Global Existing Instance ty_var.

Global Existing Instance subtyp.

Global Existing Instance ty_incap.

Inductive ty_capbnd (C : typ_refcap_label) : CapabilityBound C :=
| ty_capbnd_top G e:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_top ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_top

| ty_capbnd_bot G e:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_bot ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_bot

| ty_capbnd_typ G e A S T:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) S T) ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_top

| ty_capbnd_cap_sel G e S T:

    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap C) S T) ∶cpb⟦C⟧ T

| ty_capbnd_cap_ignore G e C' S T:
    C' <> C ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap C') S T) ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_top

| ty_capbnd_met G e m TC TZ TR:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_met m TC TZ TR) ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_top

| ty_capbnd_fld G e a T1 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_rcd (dec_fld a T1 T2) ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_top

| ty_capbnd_sel G e x B y S T T':
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_typ B S T) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ (open y T) ∶cpb⟦C⟧ T' ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_sel (avar_f x) B (avar_f y) ∶cpb⟦C⟧ T'

| ty_capbnd_rec G e T:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_bnd T ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_top

| ty_capbnd_and G e S1 T1 S2 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ S1 ∶cpb⟦C⟧ S2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T1 ∶cpb⟦C⟧ T2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_and S1 T1 ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_and S2 T2

| ty_capbnd_or G e S1 T1 S2 T2:
    G⁏e ⊢ S1 ∶cpb⟦C⟧ S2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T1 ∶cpb⟦C⟧ T2 ->
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_or S1 T1 ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_or S2 T2

| ty_capbnd_all G e S T:
    G⁏e ⊢ typ_fun S T ∶cpb⟦C⟧ typ_top

.

Global Existing Instance ty_capbnd.

Inductive viewpoint_adapt_cap: typ_refcap_label -> var -> (TypingProperty typ typ) :=
| viewpoint_adapt_cap_strip_combine C x G Go e T Tstrip Tcap:
    G§§Go⁏e ⊢ T ∶icp Tstrip ->
    G§§Go⁏e ⊢ T ∶cpb⟦C⟧ Tcap ->
    viewpoint_adapt_cap C x G Go e T (typ_and Tstrip (typ_cap_adapt C x Tcap)).

Definition viewpoint_adapt x G Go e Tf Tr :=
  match (mode_viewpoint_adaptation' typing_mode) with

  | mode_viewpoint_adaptation_same => Tf = Tr

  | mode_viewpoint_adapt_mutability => viewpoint_adapt_cap typ_refcap_mutability x G Go e Tf Tr
  end.

End WithTypingMode.

Notation "G ⁏ e ⊢ x ▷⟦ C ⟧ T1 ⟶ T2" :=
  (viewpoint_adapt_cap _ C x G objctx_empty e T1 T2)
    (at level 40, e at level 39, x at level 59, T1 at level 59, T2 at level 59).

Notation "G ⁏ e ⊢ x ▷ T1 ⟶ T2" :=
  (viewpoint_adapt _ x G objctx_empty e T1 T2)
    (at level 40, e at level 39, x at level 59, T1 at level 59, T2 at level 59).

Notation typ_objlit typing_mode T := (
  match (mode_objlit_refcaps' typing_mode) with

  | mode_objlit_refcaps_none => typ_and (typ_bnd T) typ_top

  | mode_objlit_refcaps_mutable => typ_and (typ_bnd T) (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)
  end) (only parsing).

Notation vis_var typing_mode G x := (
  (mode_has_visibility typing_mode) -> (ctx_vis G x)
  ) (only parsing).

Notation mut_var_writeable typing_mode G e x := (
  (mode_has_mutability typing_mode) -> (G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ (typ_mut_marker typ_bot) )
  ) (only parsing).

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Inductive ty_trm : Typing trm :=

| ty_trm_var : forall G e x T,
    vis_var typing_mode G x ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ trm_var (avar_f x) ∶ T

| ty_trm_apply : forall G e x z S T,
    mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
    vis_var typing_mode G x ->
    vis_var typing_mode G z ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_fun S T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ z ∶ S ->
    G⁏e ⊢ trm_apply (avar_f x) (avar_f z) ∶ open z T

| ty_trm_read : forall G e x a S T U,
    vis_var typing_mode G x ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a S T) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ▷ T ⟶ U ->
    G⁏e ⊢ trm_read (avar_f x) a ∶ U

| ty_trm_write : forall G e x y a S T,
    vis_var typing_mode G x ->
    vis_var typing_mode G y ->
    mut_var_writeable typing_mode G e x ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_fld a S T) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ y ∶ S ->
    G⁏e ⊢ trm_write (avar_f x) a (avar_f y) ∶ T

| ty_trm_call : forall G e x y m TC TZ TR,
    vis_var typing_mode G x ->
    vis_var typing_mode G y ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ typ_rcd (dec_met m TC TZ TR) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ y ∶ TZ ->
    (mode_has_sef typing_mode -> typ_indep_b 0 TC) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ x ∶ (open y TC) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ trm_call (avar_f x) m (avar_f y) ∶ open_met y x TR

| ty_trm_let : forall L G e t u T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ t ∶ T ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G § x / v_let ~ T ⁏e ⊢ open x u ∶ U) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ trm_let t u ∶ U

| ty_trm_lit : forall L G e l u T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ l ∶ T ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G § x / v_let ~ T ⁏e ⊢ open x u ∶ U) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ trm_lit l u ∶ U

| ty_trm_sub : forall G e (t : trm) T U,
    G⁏e ⊢ t ∶ T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ T <: U ->
    G⁏e ⊢ t ∶ U

with ty_lit : Typing lit :=

| ty_lit_fun : forall L G e T t U,
    mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G § x / v_par ~ T ⁏e ⊢ open x t ∶ open x U) ->
    G⁏e ⊢ lit_fun T t ∶ typ_fun T U

| ty_lit_obj : forall L G e T ds,
    (forall x, x \notin L -> G §§ (objctx_lit x T) ⁏e ⊢ (open x ds) ∶ (open x T)) ->
    typ_indep_b 0 T ->
    G⁏e ⊢ lit_obj T ds ∶ typ_objlit typing_mode T

with ty_def : DecTyping def :=

| ty_def_typ : forall L G Go e A T U,
    (forall x, x \notin L -> e ⊢ (open x T) ≈ (open x U)) ->
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ def_typ (typ_label_normal A) T ∶d dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) U U

| ty_def_fld : forall G Go e a t T,
    vis_var typing_mode (G §§& Go) t ->
    G §§& Go⁏e ⊢ t ∶ T ->
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ def_fld a (avar_f t) ∶d dec_fld a T T

| ty_def_met : forall L G Go e m t TC TZ TR,
    (forall xz, xz \notin L ->
    forall xc, xc <> xz -> xc \notin L ->
    ctx_obj_met typing_mode G Go xz TZ xc TC ⁏e ⊢ open_met xz xc t ∶ open_met xz xc TR) ->
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ def_met m t ∶d dec_met m TC TZ TR

with ty_defs: Typing defs :=

| ty_defs_one : forall G Go e d D,
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ d ∶d D ->
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ defs_cons defs_nil d ∶ typ_rcd D

| ty_defs_cons : forall G Go e ds d T D,
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ ds ∶ T ->
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ d ∶d D ->
    defs_hasnt ds (label_of d) ->
    G §§ Go⁏e ⊢ defs_cons ds d ∶ typ_and T (typ_rcd D)
.

Global Existing Instance ty_trm | 0.

Global Existing Instance ty_def | 0.

Global Existing Instance ty_lit | 1.

Global Existing Instance ty_defs | 1.

Scheme ts_ty_var_mut := Induction for ty_var Sort Prop
with   ts_subtyp     := Induction for subtyp Sort Prop
with   ts_ty_incap   := Induction for ty_incap Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme ts_mutind from ts_ty_var_mut, ts_subtyp, ts_ty_incap.

Scheme rules_trm_mut    := Induction for ty_trm Sort Prop
with   rules_lit_mut    := Induction for ty_lit Sort Prop
with   rules_def_mut    := Induction for ty_def Sort Prop
with   rules_defs_mut   := Induction for ty_defs Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme rules_mutind from rules_trm_mut, rules_lit_mut,
rules_def_mut, rules_defs_mut.

End WithTypingMode.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

End WithTypingMode.

Notation SubtypingPropery := (ctx -> renv -> typ -> typ -> Prop) (only parsing).

Module GeneralizedSubtyping.

Class AndOrSubtyping (ST: SubtypingPropery) := {
  and11 G e T U: ST G e (typ_and T U) T;
  and12 G e T U: ST G e (typ_and T U) U;
  and2 G e S T U:
    ST G e S T ->
    ST G e S U ->
    ST G e S (typ_and T U);
  or11 G e T U: ST G e T (typ_or T U);
  or12 G e T U: ST G e U (typ_or T U);
  or2 G e S T U:
    ST G e S T ->
    ST G e U T ->
    ST G e (typ_or S U) T;
  trans G e S T U:
    ST G e S T ->
    ST G e T U ->
    ST G e S U;
}.

End GeneralizedSubtyping.

Section GeneralizedSubtypingLemmata.

Context {ST} {AOS: GeneralizedSubtyping.AndOrSubtyping ST}.

End GeneralizedSubtypingLemmata.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Global Instance and_or_subtyp: GeneralizedSubtyping.AndOrSubtyping (fun G => (subtyping)  G objctx_empty) := {
  and11 := subtyp_and11 typing_mode;
  and12 := subtyp_and12 typing_mode;
  and2 := @subtyp_and2 typing_mode;
  or11 := subtyp_or11 typing_mode;
  or12 := subtyp_or12 typing_mode;
  or2 := @subtyp_or2 typing_mode;
  trans := @subtyp_trans typing_mode;
}.

End WithTypingMode.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import AbstractSyntax TypingMode GeneralTyping EnvCorrespondence TFree ConfigVarkinds Defs RecordDefs.

Inductive defs_update : defs -> fld_label -> var -> defs -> Prop :=
| defs_update_var : forall ds a t x,
    defs_update (defs_cons ds (def_fld a t)) a x (defs_cons ds (def_fld a (avar_f x)))
| defs_update_push : forall ds d a x ds',
    defs_update ds a x ds' ->
    label_of d <> (label_fld a) ->
    defs_update (defs_cons ds d) a x (defs_cons ds' d).

Definition heap_update (s : heap) (x : var) (a : fld_label) (y : var) (s' : heap) :=
  ok s /\
  ok s' /\
  (dom s) = (dom s') /\
  (forall z v, z <> x ->
          binds z v s ->
          binds z v s') /\
  exists ds ds', binds x (item_obj ds) s /\
              defs_update ds a y ds' /\
              binds x (item_obj ds') s'.

Require Import RecordTypes InertContext HeapCorrespondence.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

End WithTypingMode.

Require Import LibExtra Vars Terms Stack Heap Env SyntaxClasses.

Inductive config: Type := config_mk (t:trm) (s:stack) (S:heap) (e:renv) (Lv: fset var): config.

Notation "t ; s ; Sigma ; e ; Lv" :=
  (config_mk t s Sigma e Lv) (at level 39, s, Sigma, e at level 38, Lv at level 38) : syntax_scope.

Definition config_heap C := (
  match C with
  _ ; _ ; Sc ; _ ; _ => Sc
  end ).

Definition config_env C := (
  match C with
  _ ; _ ; _ ; e ; _ => e
  end ).

Definition config_fv C := (
  match C with
  _ ; _ ; _ ; _ ; Lv => Lv
  end ).

Notation fv_renv e := ((@dom var e) \u (fv_env e)).

Notation fv_config c :=
  match c with
  | (t ; s ; Sigma ; e ; Lv) =>
    (@fv trm _ t) \u (@fv stack _ s) \u (fv_heap Sigma)
      \u (fv_renv e) \u Lv
  end.

Notation fresh_in_config l c := (fresh (fv_config c) (length l) l).

Definition nothing_fresh_in_config A {AF: FreeVar A} (a:A) c :=
  (fv a) \c fv_config c.

Notation vars_conf xs C := (
    from_list xs \c fv_config C
  ) (only parsing).

Definition vars_conf_unique xs C := (
    fresh \{} (length xs) xs /\
    vars_conf xs C
  ).

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import Coq.Bool.Bool.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import Vars Labels TransformCollect Types.

Inductive trm : Set :=
  | trm_var  : avar -> trm
  | trm_read  : avar -> fld_label -> trm
  | trm_apply  : avar -> avar -> trm
  | trm_let  : trm -> trm -> trm
  | trm_lit  : lit -> trm -> trm
  | trm_write  : avar -> fld_label -> avar -> trm
  | trm_call: avar -> met_label -> avar -> trm

with lit : Set :=
  | lit_fun : typ -> trm -> lit
  | lit_obj  : typ -> defs -> lit

with def : Set :=
  | def_typ  : typ_label -> typ -> def
  | def_fld  : fld_label -> avar -> def
  | def_met  : met_label -> trm -> def

with defs : Set :=
  | defs_nil : defs
  | defs_cons : defs -> def -> defs.

Scheme trm_mut  := Induction for trm  Sort Prop
with   lit_mut  := Induction for lit  Sort Prop
with   def_mut  := Induction for def  Sort Prop
with   defs_mut := Induction for defs Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme trm_mutind from trm_mut, lit_mut, def_mut, defs_mut.

Fixpoint open_rec_trm (k: nat) (u: var) (t: trm): trm :=
  match t with
  | trm_var a      => trm_var (open_rec k u a)
  | trm_read v m    => trm_read (open_rec k u v) m
  | trm_apply f a    => trm_apply (open_rec k u f) (open_rec k u a)
  | trm_let t1 t2  => trm_let (open_rec_trm k u t1) (open_rec_trm (S k) u t2)
  | trm_lit l t => trm_lit (open_rec_lit k u l) (open_rec_trm (S k) u t)
  | trm_write v m v2 => trm_write (open_rec k u v) m (open_rec k u v2)
  | trm_call v m v2 => trm_call (open_rec k u v) m (open_rec k u v2)
  end with
open_rec_lit (k: nat) (u: var) (l: lit): lit :=
  match l with
  | lit_fun T t => lit_fun (open_rec k u T) (open_rec_trm (S k) u t)
  | lit_obj T ds =>
    lit_obj
      (open_rec (S k) u T)
      (open_rec_defs (S k) u ds)

  end with
open_rec_def (k: nat) (u: var) (d: def): def :=
  match d with
  | def_typ L T => def_typ L (open_rec (S k) u T)
  | def_fld m v => def_fld m (open_rec k u v)
  | def_met m e => def_met m (open_rec_trm (S (S k)) u e)
  end with
open_rec_defs (k: nat) (u: var) (ds: defs): defs :=
  match ds with
  | defs_nil       => defs_nil
  | defs_cons tl d => defs_cons (open_rec_defs k u tl) (open_rec_def k u d)
  end.

Instance TrmOpenable : Openable trm := open_rec_trm.

Instance LitOpenable : Openable lit := open_rec_lit.

Instance DefOpenable : Openable def := open_rec_def.

Instance DefsOpenable : Openable defs := open_rec_defs.

Fixpoint fv_trm (t: trm) : vars :=
  match t with
  | trm_var a         => (fv a)
  | trm_read x m       => (fv x)
  | trm_apply f a       => (fv f) \u (fv a)
  | trm_let t1 t2     => (fv_trm t1) \u (fv_trm t2)
  | trm_lit l t       => (fv_lit l) \u (fv_trm t)
  | trm_write x m y     => (fv x) \u (fv y)
  | trm_call x m y => (fv x) \u (fv y)
  end with
fv_lit (l: lit) : vars :=
  match l with
  | lit_fun T e    => (fv T) \u (fv_trm e)
  | lit_obj T ds => (fv T) \u (fv_defs ds)
  end with
fv_def (d: def) : vars :=
  match d with
  | def_typ _ T     => (fv T)
  | def_fld _ v     => (fv v)
  | def_met _ t     => (fv_trm t)
  end with
fv_defs(ds: defs) : vars :=
  match ds with
  | defs_nil         => \{}
  | defs_cons tl d   => (fv_defs tl) \u (fv_def d)
  end.

Instance TrmFreeVar : FreeVar trm := fv_trm.

Instance LitFreeVar : FreeVar lit := fv_lit.

Instance DefFreeVar : FreeVar def := fv_def.

Instance DefsFreeVar : FreeVar defs := fv_defs.

Fixpoint subst_trm (z: var) (u: var) (t: trm) : trm :=
  match t with
  | trm_var x        => trm_var (subst_var z u x)
  | trm_read x1 L     => trm_read (subst_var z u x1) L
  | trm_apply x1 x2    => trm_apply (subst_var z u x1) (subst_var z u x2)
  | trm_let t1 t2    => trm_let (subst_trm z u t1) (subst_trm z u t2)
  | trm_lit l t      => trm_lit (subst_lit z u l) (subst_trm z u t)
  | trm_write x1 L x2  => trm_write (subst_var z u x1) L (subst_var z u x2)
  | trm_call x1 L x2  => trm_call (subst_var z u x1) L (subst_var z u x2)

  | trm_let t1 t2     => (fv_trm t1) \u (fv_trm t2)
  | trm_lit l t       => (fv_lit l) \u (fv_trm t)
  | trm_write x m y     => (fv x) \u (fv y)
  | trm_call x m y => (fv x) \u (fv y)
  end with
fv_lit (l: lit) : vars :=
  match l with
  | lit_fun T e    => (fv T) \u (fv_trm e)
  | lit_obj T ds => (fv T) \u (fv_defs ds)
  end with
fv_def (d: def) : vars :=
  match d with
  | def_typ _ T     => (fv T)
  | def_fld _ v     => (fv v)
  | def_met _ t     => (fv_trm t)
  end with
fv_defs(ds: defs) : vars :=
  match ds with
  | defs_nil         => \{}
  | defs_cons tl d   => (fv_defs tl) \u (fv_def d)
  end.

Instance TrmFreeVar : FreeVar trm := fv_trm.

Instance LitFreeVar : FreeVar lit := fv_lit.

Instance DefFreeVar : FreeVar def := fv_def.

Instance DefsFreeVar : FreeVar defs := fv_defs.

Fixpoint subst_trm (z: var) (u: var) (t: trm) : trm :=
  match t with
  | trm_var x        => trm_var (subst_var z u x)
  | trm_read x1 L     => trm_read (subst_var z u x1) L
  | trm_apply x1 x2    => trm_apply (subst_var z u x1) (subst_var z u x2)
  | trm_let t1 t2    => trm_let (subst_trm z u t1) (subst_trm z u t2)
  | trm_lit l t      => trm_lit (subst_lit z u l) (subst_trm z u t)
  | trm_write x1 L x2  => trm_write (subst_var z u x1) L (subst_var z u x2)
  | trm_call x1 L x2  => trm_call (subst_var z u x1) L (subst_var z u x2)

`closed t := forall n x, open_rec n x t = t`. For trm_call (avar_f w1) m (avar_f w2), open_rec n x will replace bound vars (avar_b) but avar_f stays, so closed holds trivially for any term with only free vars! Because open_rec only substitutes bound variables. Indeed `closed` here means "no free variables"? Wait open_rec n x (avar_f w) = avar_f w (unchanged), and for avar_b k, if k = n then avar_f x else avar_b k. `closed a := forall n x, open_rec n x a = a` means no avar_b at any depth, i.e., all variables are free (named). Hmm, that's the locally nameless convention: closed = no locally-bound variables (all free). So yes, the call term is closed. OK.

So no contradiction there.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import AbstractSyntax TypingMode GeneralTyping EnvCorrespondence Visibility TFree ConfigVarkinds Deref HeapInstantiate Indep RecordTypes InertContext RecordDefs Equivalence ConfigNotations.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

Inductive ty_item_s : ctx -> renv -> heap -> var -> Prop :=

| ty_item_fun_s : forall G e s x S t L T,
    mode_has_fun typing_mode ->
    ctx_binds x (typ_fun S T) G ->
    binds x (item_fun t) s ->
    (forall x, x \notin L ->
      G § x / v_par ~ S ⁏e ⊢ open x t ∶ open x T) ->
    all_tfree_k G t v_ref ->
    ty_item_s G e s x
| ty_item_obj_s : forall G e s x U S ds T,
    ctx_binds x T G ->
    binds x (item_obj ds) s ->
    T = typ_objref U S ->
    G §§ (objctx_heap x U) ⁏e ⊢ ds ∶ (open x U) ->
    defs_varkinds G ds ->
    ty_item_s G e s x.

Definition heap_correspond (G : ctx) (e: renv) (s : heap) : Prop :=
  ctx_ok G /\
  ctx_weakens G /\
  ok s /\
  ok e /\
  ctx_kdom v_loc G = dom s /\
  ctx_kdom v_ref G = dom e /\
  renv_corr G e /\
  (forall x,
      x \in dom s ->
      ty_item_s G e s x).

End WithTypingMode.

Arguments heap_correspond {typing_mode}.

Notation inert_G_for_item G w y T := (G § y / v_loc ~ T § w / v_ref ~ T).

Notation inert_G_for_obj G w y T S := (inert_G_for_item G w y (typ_objref T S)).

Notation heap_prefix S1 S2 := (exists S1', S2 = concat S1 S1').

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra.

Require Import Coq.Program.Equality.

Require Import AbstractSyntax TypingMode GeneralTyping Indep Equivalence.

Inductive record_dec : dec -> Prop :=
| rd_typ : forall A T, record_dec (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) T T)
| rd_typb : forall A T, record_dec (dec_typ (typ_label_normal A) typ_bot T)
| rd_fld : forall a T, record_dec (dec_fld a T T)
| rd_met : forall m TC TZ TR, record_dec (dec_met m TC TZ TR)
.

Inductive record_typ : typ -> fset label -> Prop :=
| rt_one : forall D l,
  record_dec D ->
  l = label_of D ->
  record_typ (typ_rcd D) \{l}
| rt_cons: forall T ls D l,
  record_typ T ls ->
  record_dec D ->
  l = label_of D ->
  l \notin ls ->
  record_typ (typ_and T (typ_rcd D)) (union ls \{l}).

Definition record_type T := exists ls, record_typ T ls.

Inductive refcap_dec: dec -> Prop :=
  | refcap_dec_typb lt TU:
    refcap_dec (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap lt) typ_bot TU).

Inductive refcap_typ: typ -> fset label -> Prop :=
  | refcap_typ_top:
      refcap_typ typ_top \{}
  | refcap_typ_one D l:
      refcap_dec D ->
      l = label_of D ->
      refcap_typ (typ_rcd D) \{l}
  | refcap_typ_cons T ls D l:
      refcap_typ T ls ->
      refcap_dec D ->
      l = label_of D ->
      l \notin ls ->
      refcap_typ (typ_and T (typ_rcd D)) (union ls \{l}).

Definition refcap_type T := exists ls, refcap_typ T ls.

Inductive record_has: typ -> dec -> Prop :=
| rh_one : forall D,
    record_has (typ_rcd D) D
| rh_andl : forall T U D,
    record_has T D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D
| rh_andr : forall T U D,
    record_has U D ->
    record_has (typ_and T U) D.

Section WithTypingMode.

Context (typing_mode: Mode).

End WithTypingMode.

content.thinking:
Typeclass resolution picks the local `typing_mode` for `⊢` in the hypotheses (because it's the only Mode in context). And ty_config uses typing_mode as implicit arg. Good.

Now, to prove the theorem. We need to reason about reduction sequences. Let's think about a strategy:

The theorem is essentially: if we're k steps into a call's execution of a pure method, then either the call returned (frame ended) before step k, or the heap is unchanged.

The "frame" concept: `frame_end_in c1 j c3` requires:
- c1 ⊣ j ↦* c3
- frame_within c1 j (for all k ≤ j, c1 ⊣k↦* C4 -> stack_suffix (config_stack c1) (config_stack C4))
- config_stack c3 = config_stack c1
- exists w3, config_trm c3 = trm_var (avar_f w3)

Meaning after j steps, the computation returns to a variable with the same stack. In the call semantics, a call opens the method body *without pushing a stack frame*! So how do we detect the call returning? The term eventually evaluates to a variable (when the method body is a variable or a let that returns). Hmm, `frame_end_in` for a call doesn't use a stack frame; it just means the whole term reduces to a variable with unchanged stack. But `frame_within` requires stack suffix at all intermediate steps, which holds if no stack changes (only let pushes frames append). Actually stack_suffix fs1 fs2 means fs2 = stack_append fs3 fs1, i.e., fs1 is a suffix of fs2? Let's check stack_append order. In red_let_push, term (let s t) with stack fs goes to (s; stack_cons (frame_let t) fs). So the stack grows by consing on front. `stack_suffix fs1 fs2 := exists fs3, fs2 = stack_append fs3 fs1`. Need to know stack_append: `Fixpoint stack_append (fs1 fs2: stack) := match fs1 with nil => fs2 | cons f fs => stack_cons f (stack_append fs fs2) end`. So stack_append fs3 fs1 = fs3 ++ fs1. So stack_suffix fs1 fs2 means fs2 = fs3 ++ fs1, i.e., fs1 is suffix of fs2. In red_let_push, fs -> cons frame fs, so fs is suffix. In red_let_var, the stack has (frame_let t)::fs and reduces to fs, so old stack is not a suffix of new. Hmm, so during a call's evaluation, if the method body contains a let and it returns, the stack shrinks, and frame_within would not hold after that. But frame_end is meant to catch exactly the moment the method call body finishes? Hmm.

Actually, wait. `frame_within C1 m` says for all k <= m, if C1 ⊣k↦* C4 then stack_suffix (config_stack C1) (config_stack C4). If the method body pushes and pops frames, then during execution the stack might be longer (suffix holds), but when popping, we get back to the original stack (suffix holds trivially, since fs = nil ++ fs). So stack_suffix holds for all intermediate states as long as we never pop *below* the original stack. Since the call starts with the entire stack config_stack c1 = fs, and the body operates on top of fs, it can push and pop, but the original fs stays as suffix. So frame_within holds as long as execution of the call doesn't return to the caller's continuation. But there is no continuation frame pushed for a call—calls are tail-like: the term is replaced by the body. So when the body finishes evaluating to a variable, the "call" is done. `frame_end_in` characterizes that with config_trm c3 = trm_var.

OK so the statement: for a pure call, while it's still running (hasn't reached a variable), the heap is unchanged. If it reaches a variable within j<k steps, first disjunct. This makes sense.

Now, how to prove it? We need to analyze the reduction sequence. Without subject reduction lemmas, we must prove heap preservation directly from typing facts. But the hypothesis `ty_config` gives us typing of the initial term only. We don't get typing of intermediate configs! Unless we prove a preservation theorem ourselves. That's the full soundness. Hmm.

Wait, maybe the heap cannot change during a call *regardless of typing*? Let's examine the reduction rules and the shape of the initial term. The initial term is `trm_call (avar_f w1) m (avar_f w2)`. First step must be red_call (if any), where the term becomes `open w2 (open_rec 1 w1 t)` for the method body t from the heap. After that, arbitrary computation of the body. The body can include writes. But the body came from a heap object that existed before. Could the body have been created during this call? No, it's in the initial heap. But could it write? Yes, if t contains a write to a field of an object in the heap.

However! The typing hypothesis might not even be needed for the *call* part, but for purity. Let's see whether the method body t in the heap is constrained by `[w1 : typ_rcd (dec_met m typ_nocap TZv typ_top)]`. We only know w1's type has method m with capability typ_nocap. In the calculus, capability typ_nocap presumably encodes "the method is pure". So any object typed with this method type has a body whose writes are to fresh objects only? Wait no—modes with incap/visibility etc. constrain method bodies.

Actually let's reconsider. The type `dec_met m TC TZ TR`: TC is the capability type of the method (the "self" type under which the body is typed), TZ is the argument type, TR is the return type. `typ_nocap` means the method is granted no capability (cannot mutate). `ty_def_met` types the body under context `ctx_obj_met typing_mode G Go xz TZ xc TC`. Let's look at `ctx_obj_met` in Objctx.v.

Inductive typ_indep: avar -> typ -> Prop :=
| typ_indep_nulary v T:
  typ_nulary T -> typ_indep v T

| typ_indep_and v t1 t2:
    typ_indep v t1->
    typ_indep v t2->
    typ_indep v (typ_and t1 t2)
| typ_indep_or v t1 t2:
    typ_indep v t1->
    typ_indep v t2->
    typ_indep v (typ_or t1 t2)
| typ_indep_fld v a t1 t2:
    typ_indep v t1->
    typ_indep v t2->
    typ_indep v (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t1 t2))
| typ_indep_typ_f v a t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t1->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t2->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) (typ_rcd (dec_typ a t1 t2))
| typ_indep_typ_b n a t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_b (S n)) t1->
    typ_indep (avar_b (S n)) t2->
    typ_indep (avar_b n) (typ_rcd (dec_typ a t1 t2))
| typ_indep_fun_f v t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t1 ->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t2 ->
    typ_indep (avar_f v) (typ_fun t1 t2)
| typ_indep_fun_b n t1 t2:
    typ_indep (avar_b n) t1 ->
    typ_indep (avar_b (S n)) t2 ->
    typ_indep (avar_b n) (typ_fun t1 t2)
| typ_indep_sel(v v1 v2: avar)(l: typ_label):
    v <> v1 ->
    v <> v2 ->
    typ_indep v (typ_sel v1 l v2)

    v <> v2 ->
    typ_indep v (typ_sel v1 (typ_label_normal l) v2)
| typ_indep_bnd_f v t:
    typ_indep (avar_f v) t ->

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Inductive avar : Set :=
  | avar_b : nat -> avar
  | avar_f : var -> avar.

Notation avars := (list avar).

Instance VarSubstVar : SubstVar var :=
  fun x y z => If z = x then y else z.

Instance VarSealable: Sealable var :=
  fun n x y => y.

Instance VarOpenable : Openable var :=
  fun n x a => a.

Instance VarFreeVar : FreeVar var := singleton (A:=var).

Instance VarAbstractSyntax :
  AbstractSyntax VarOpenable VarFreeVar VarSubstVar := {}.

Instance AvarOpenable : Openable avar :=
  fun n x a =>
    match a with
    | avar_b i => If n = i then avar_f x else avar_b i
    | avar_f y => avar_f y
    end.

Instance AvarFreeVar : FreeVar avar :=
  fun a =>
    match a with
    | avar_b i => \{}
    | avar_f x => \{x}
    end.

Instance AvarSubstVar : SubstVar avar :=
  fun (x: var) (y: var) (a: avar) =>
    match a with
    | avar_b i => avar_b i
    | avar_f z => (avar_f (If z = x then y else z))
    end.

Instance AvarAbstractSyntax :
  AbstractSyntax AvarOpenable AvarFreeVar AvarSubstVar := {}.

Instance AvarSealable : Sealable avar :=
  fun n x a =>
    match a with
    | avar_b i => If n <= i then avar_f x else avar_b i
    | avar_f y => avar_f y
    end.

Instance AvarDecideFv : DecideFv AvarAbstractSyntax :=
  fun x a =>
    match a with
    | avar_b i => false
    | avar_f y => (If x = y then true else false)
    end.

Instance AvarClosing : Closing AvarAbstractSyntax :=
  fun (n : nat) (x : var) (a : avar) =>
    match a with
    | avar_b i => avar_b i
    | avar_f y => (If y = x then avar_b n else avar_f y)
    end.

Section VarSubstVar.

Context `{AS: AbstractSyntax}.

Context {SF: SubstFresh AS}.

Context {FS: FvSubstCases AS}.

Context {SC: SubstCommut AS}.

Context {ASOC: SubstOpenCommut AS}.

Context {SI: SubstId AS}.

End VarSubstVar.

Inductive varkind: Set :=
| v_loc: varkind
| v_ref: varkind
| v_par: varkind
| v_self: varkind
| v_let: varkind
| v_recv: varkind
.

Inductive varkind_abstract: varkind -> Prop :=
| v_abstract_let: varkind_abstract v_let
| v_abstract_par: varkind_abstract v_par
| v_abstract_self: varkind_abstract v_self
| v_abstract_recv: varkind_abstract v_recv
.

Claim: For any reduction sequence starting from a call term, if it doesn't reach a "frame end", then the heap only changes at objects that were... hmm.

Alternative: Maybe we can show that the first step (red_call) is the *only* step possible before returning a variable? No—after the call step, the term is the body, which can be complex.

Let's test the simpler question: Is the theorem true if we drop all typing hypotheses and use only the shape? Construct a concrete semantic counterexample: c1 = (call w1 m w2; nil; Sigma; e; Lv), where Sigma has y1 -> item_obj [def_met m (write x f y2)] and y2 -> item_obj [def_fld f (avar_f old)]. e: w1->y1, x->y2, y2'? Let's say the body is `trm_write (avar_f x) f (avar_f z)` where x maps to y2 (pre-existing). After red_call with opens (body has no bound vars, so stays same), we get config (write x f z; nil; Sigma; e; Lv). Then red_write: heap_update Sigma y2 f yArg Sigma', changing y2. Then final c4 has changed y2. For k=2, first disjunct would need frame_end_in c1 j c3 with j<2: j=1 gives c3 = (write x f z;...), term not a var. j=0 impossible. So first disjunct false. Second: subheap_unchanged Sigma Sigma' false because y2 changed. So theorem false without typing. So typing is essential.

Thus we need to use typing to rule out such bodies. The specific typing hypotheses are only about the *initial* config and w1's method type, not about body t directly, except through heap_correspond: the heap object at y1's type in G and its item's body typing. This gives the method body purity.

1	Set Implicit Arguments.

3	Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.
4	
5	Require Import AbstractSyntax Context Defs Heap.
6	
7	Class TFree(A : Set) := tfree: var -> A -> Prop.
8	
9	Inductive tfree_trm: TFree trm :=
10	
11	| tfree_trm_var v:
12	  tfree_trm v (trm_var (avar_f v))
13	
14	| tfree_trm_read v1 l:
15	  tfree_trm v1 (trm_read (avar_f v1) l)
16	
17	| tfree_trm_apply_l v1 a2:
18	  tfree_trm v1 (trm_apply (avar_f v1) a2)
19	| tfree_trm_apply_r a1 v2:
20	  tfree_trm v2 (trm_apply a1 (avar_f v2))
21	
22	| tfree_trm_let_l v t1 t2:
23	  tfree_trm v t1 ->
24	  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)
25	| tfree_trm_let_r v t1 t2:
26	  tfree_trm v t2 ->
27	  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)
28	
29	| tfree_trm_lit_l v t1 t2:
30	  tfree_lit v t1 ->
31	  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)
32	| tfree_trm_lit_r v t1 t2:
33	  tfree_trm v t2 ->
34	  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)
35	
36	| tfree_trm_write_l v1 a2 l:
37	  tfree_trm v1 (trm_write (avar_f v1) l a2)
38	| tfree_trm_write_r a1 v2 l:
39	  tfree_trm v2 (trm_write a1 l (avar_f v2))
40	
41	| tfree_trm_call_l v1 a2 l:
42	  tfree_trm v1 (trm_call (avar_f v1) l a2)
43	| tfree_trm_call_r a1 v2 l:
44	  tfree_trm v2 (trm_call a1 l (avar_f v2))
45	
46	with tfree_lit: TFree lit :=
47	
48	| tfree_lit_fun v t T:
49	  tfree_trm v t ->
50	  tfree_lit v (lit_fun T t)
51	| tfree_lit_obj v t T:
52	  tfree_defs v t ->
53	  tfree_lit v (lit_obj T t)
54	
55	with tfree_def: TFree def :=
56	
57	| tfree_def_trm v l:
58	  tfree_def v (def_fld l (avar_f v))
59	
60	| tfree_def_met v t l:
61	  tfree_trm v t ->
62	  tfree_def v (def_met l t)
63	
64	with tfree_defs: TFree defs :=
65	
66	| tfree_defs_cons_l v d ds:
67	  tfree_defs v ds ->
68	  tfree_defs v (defs_cons ds d)
69	| tfree_defs_cons_r v d ds:
70	  tfree_def v d ->
71	  tfree_defs v (defs_cons ds d)
72	.
73	
74	Scheme tfree_trm_mut    := Induction for tfree_trm Sort Prop
75	with   tfree_lit_mut    := Induction for tfree_lit Sort Prop
76	with   tfree_def_mut    := Induction for tfree_def Sort Prop
77	with   tfree_defs_mut   := Induction for tfree_defs Sort Prop.
78	
79	Combined Scheme tfree_mutind from tfree_trm_mut, tfree_lit_mut,
80	tfree_def_mut, tfree_defs_mut.
81	
82	Inductive tfree_stack: TFree stack :=
83	
84	| tfree_stack_cons_l v t st:
85	  tfree_trm v t ->
86	  tfree_stack v (stack_cons (frame_let t) st)
87	| tfree_stack_cons_r v f st:
88	  tfree_stack v st ->
89	  tfree_stack v (stack_cons f st)
90	.

93

96	Existing Instance tfree_def.
97	
98	Existing Instance tfree_defs.
99	
100	Existing Instance tfree_stack.

102	Definition all_tfree_k {A: Set} {AT: TFree A} G (t:A) vk :=
103	  forall v, tfree v t -> ctx_k G v vk.

105	Notation all_tfree_k_trm := (@all_tfree_k trm _).
106

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Context Defs Heap.

Class TFree(A : Set) := tfree: var -> A -> Prop.

Inductive tfree_trm: TFree trm :=

| tfree_trm_var v:
  tfree_trm v (trm_var (avar_f v))

| tfree_trm_read v1 l:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_read (avar_f v1) l)

| tfree_trm_apply_l v1 a2:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_apply (avar_f v1) a2)
| tfree_trm_apply_r a1 v2:
  tfree_trm v2 (trm_apply a1 (avar_f v2))

| tfree_trm_let_l v t1 t2:
  tfree_trm v t1 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)
| tfree_trm_let_r v t1 t2:
  tfree_trm v t2 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_let t1 t2)

| tfree_trm_lit_l v t1 t2:
  tfree_lit v t1 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)
| tfree_trm_lit_r v t1 t2:
  tfree_trm v t2 ->
  tfree_trm v (trm_lit t1 t2)

| tfree_trm_write_l v1 a2 l:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_write (avar_f v1) l a2)
| tfree_trm_write_r a1 v2 l:
  tfree_trm v2 (trm_write a1 l (avar_f v2))

| tfree_trm_call_l v1 a2 l:
  tfree_trm v1 (trm_call (avar_f v1) l a2)
| tfree_trm_call_r a1 v2 l:
  tfree_trm v2 (trm_call a1 l (avar_f v2))

with tfree_lit: TFree lit :=

| tfree_lit_fun v t T:
  tfree_trm v t ->
  tfree_lit v (lit_fun T t)
| tfree_lit_obj v t T:
  tfree_defs v t ->
  tfree_lit v (lit_obj T t)

with tfree_def: TFree def :=

| tfree_def_trm v l:
  tfree_def v (def_fld l (avar_f v))

| tfree_def_met v t l:
  tfree_trm v t ->
  tfree_def v (def_met l t)

with tfree_defs: TFree defs :=

| tfree_defs_cons_l v d ds:
  tfree_defs v ds ->
  tfree_defs v (defs_cons ds d)
| tfree_defs_cons_r v d ds:
  tfree_def v d ->
  tfree_defs v (defs_cons ds d)
.

Scheme tfree_trm_mut    := Induction for tfree_trm Sort Prop
with   tfree_lit_mut    := Induction for tfree_lit Sort Prop
with   tfree_def_mut    := Induction for tfree_def Sort Prop
with   tfree_defs_mut   := Induction for tfree_defs Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme tfree_mutind from tfree_trm_mut, tfree_lit_mut,
tfree_def_mut, tfree_defs_mut.

Inductive tfree_stack: TFree stack :=

| tfree_stack_cons_l v t st:
  tfree_trm v t ->
  tfree_stack v (stack_cons (frame_let t) st)
| tfree_stack_cons_r v f st:
  tfree_stack v st ->
  tfree_stack v (stack_cons f st)
.

Existing Instance tfree_trm.

Existing Instance tfree_lit.

Existing Instance tfree_def.

Existing Instance tfree_defs.

Existing Instance tfree_stack.

Definition all_tfree_k {A: Set} {AT: TFree A} G (t:A) vk :=
  forall v, tfree v t -> ctx_k G v vk.

Notation all_tfree_k_trm := (@all_tfree_k trm _).

Notation all_tfree_k_def := (@all_tfree_k def _).

Notation all_tfree_k_defs := (@all_tfree_k defs _).

Notation all_tfree_k_stack := (@all_tfree_k stack _).

Definition TFreeInFV (A: Set) (AT: TFree A) {AF: FreeVar A} :=
  forall v t,
    tfree v t ->
    v \in fv t.

Local Definition TFreeOpenInvInd (A: Set) (AT: TFree A) {AO: Openable A} :=
  forall v t,
    tfree v t ->
    forall k x tR,
      t = (open_rec k x tR) ->
      tfree v tR \/ v = x.

Class TFreeOpenInv(A : Set)(AT: TFree A){AO: Openable A} :=
  tfree_open_inv v x (t:A) n:
    tfree v (open_rec n x t) ->
    tfree v t \/ v = x
.

Local Definition TFreeOpenInd (A: Set) (AT: TFree A) {AO: Openable A} :=
  forall v t,
    tfree v t ->
    forall k x,
    tfree v (open_rec k x t).

Class TFreeOpen(A : Set)(AT: TFree A){AO: Openable A} :=
  tfree_open v x (t:A) n:
    tfree v t ->
    tfree v (open_rec n x t).

Section TFreeOpenLemmata.

Context (A: Set) {AT: TFree A} {AO: Openable A} {ATO: TFreeOpenInv AT}.

End TFreeOpenLemmata.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import AbstractSyntax Defs GeneralTyping Equivalence Indep.

Fixpoint deref_base A (su: SubstVar A) (e: renv) (X: A): A :=
  match e with
  | nil => X
  | cons (w,y) ys => (deref_base su ys (subst_var w y X))
  end.

Class Deref A :=
  deref (e: renv) (a: A): A.

Instance deref_var: Deref var := deref_base VarSubstVar.

Instance deref_avar: Deref avar := deref_base AvarSubstVar.

Instance deref_def: Deref def :=
fun e d => match d with
| def_fld l x => def_fld l (deref e x)
| def_met l t => def_met l t
| def_typ l T => def_typ l T
end.

Fixpoint deref_defs_fix(e: renv)(ds: defs) :=
match ds with
| defs_nil => defs_nil
| defs_cons ds d => defs_cons (deref_defs_fix e ds) (deref_def e d)
end.

Instance deref_defs: Deref defs := deref_defs_fix.

Class DerefInFv (A: Set) (AD: Deref A) (AF: FreeVar A):=
  deref_in_fv x e (d: A):
    x \in fv (deref e d) ->
    x \in fv d \/ x \in fv_env e.

Now, the call typing: from w1 : target record, choose TC in ty_trm_call = typ_nocap? Then need w1 : open w2 typ_nocap = typ_nocap. Impossible (B <: typ_nocap fails). Choose TC=typ_top: need w1 : typ_top (yes). So a valid call exists. The call's method capability as typed is typ_top, but the hypothesis says the method as viewed has typ_nocap. Both views. The actual declared is typ_nocap. Hmm, but `ty_trm_call`'s TC is the capability it uses for typing the result and the receiver constraint. If TC=typ_top, the sef requirement is typ_indep typ_top (fine), and the method type chosen has capability typ_top. But the *actual* w1's method (from U) has typ_nocap. For the call rule to use TC=typ_top, it needs w1 : typ_rcd(dec_met m typ_top TZ TR) for some TZ, TR. Does w1 have that type? From U = dec_met typ_nocap typ_top typ_top, subtyping to dec_met typ_top ... requires target cap typ_top <: source cap typ_nocap (premise), i.e., typ_top <: typ_nocap — impossible! So we CANNOT view the method at capability typ_top. Subtyping capability is contravariant in the right way: target cap <: source cap. Target typ_top <: source typ_nocap fails. So the call's TC must satisfy TC <: TC_src = typ_nocap. Thus TC is a subtype of typ_nocap! Then B <: open y TC. Since TC <: typ_nocap, and open y TC is a type... B <: open y TC. Hmm! If TC <: typ_nocap, then open y TC <: open y typ_nocap = typ_nocap. We need B <: open y TC. Is that possible? B = typ_and (typ_bnd U) (mut_marker). To subtype open y TC where TC <: typ_nocap... Types below typ_nocap: typ_bot, typ_nocap (refl), and maybe typ_and/or involving them, and `typ_and typ_nocap (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)` (but that's <: typ_bot only in complement modes). B is not below typ_nocap. So B <: open y TC fails! Therefore **the call typing is impossible**: TC must be <: typ_nocap (from viewing the actual method capability typ_nocap as target), but then B <: open y TC fails. Unless TC is something like typ_bot (TC <: typ_nocap) and open y TC = typ_bot; B <: typ_bot? No.

Wait, but is the receiver type in the call rule necessarily derived from the *same* U as the hypothesis's view? The call rule's receiver type record has capability TC_call. w1 has both the target record (cap typ_nocap) and the call record (cap TC_call). Both are views of the same underlying B via subtyping. If TC_src is the declared capability, then:
- target view: typ_nocap <: TC_src.
- call view: TC_call <: TC_src.
No direct relation between typ_nocap and TC_call. The call rule also requires B <: open w2 TC_call. This is the crux. B (objref) <: open w2 TC_call. Which types can be supertypes of B? B = typ_and (typ_bnd U) S. Supertypes include:
- typ_top
- typ_and of supertypes: B <: typ_and X Y iff B <: X and B <: Y. So typ_and typ_top typ_top.
- typ_or containing a supertype: e.g., typ_or typ_top X.
- Anything B structurally subtypes: B <: typ_bnd U (via and11), and B <: S (via and12). Also B <: open w1 U (via rec elim? that's a typing rule, not subtyping, but tc could then be).
- open w2 TC_call could be typ_bnd U, S, typ_top, etc.
So TC_call could be typ_bnd U (if open w2 (typ_bnd U) = typ_bnd U, since closed/indep), or S (mut_marker typ_bot!), or typ_top, etc. The sef condition requires typ_indep_b 0 TC_call. typ_bnd U is independent (U independent). S = typ_mut_marker typ_bot is independent. So TC_call = typ_mut_marker typ_bot is possible as far as independence. But also the call view must satisfy TC_call <: TC_src, where TC_src is the declared capability, and the target view gives typ_nocap <: TC_src. If TC_call = typ_mut_marker typ_bot, then typ_mut_marker typ_bot <: TC_src. Combined with typ_nocap <: TC_src. Is there a source capability TC_src that is a supertype of both typ_nocap and typ_mut_marker typ_bot? E.g., TC_src = typ_top. Then the declared method capability is typ_top. But wait, can a method declared with capability typ_top have a body that... and can `typ_nocap <: typ_top` yes. So TC_src = typ_top works. Then both views are valid if:
- target: typ_nocap <: typ_top ✓ (arg TZv <: source arg too; target ret top).
- call: typ_mut_marker typ_bot <: typ_top ✓, arg TZ_call <: source arg, and B <: open w2 (typ_mut_marker typ_bot) = typ_mut_marker typ_bot. Is B <: typ_mut_marker typ_bot? B = typ_and (typ_bnd U) S with S = typ_mut_marker typ_bot for v_loc! B <: S via and12! YES! So B <: open w2 TC_call holds with TC_call = typ_mut_marker typ_bot!

So the call is typable with TC_call = typ_mut_marker typ_bot, source declared capability TC_src = typ_top. Then the body is typed under capability TC_src = typ_top (the declared). Hmm, so the receiver xc has capability typ_top, not mutability. But wait, the *call* rule's TC is used for the call's result type and the receiver requirement; it doesn't dictate the callee's actual typing. The callee executes with the declared capability typ_top. Still not writable.

But hold on: the call rule's sef condition `typ_indep_b 0 TC_call` holds for mut_marker bot. The *source* declared capability TC_src = typ_top is independent. So the call is allowed. The body is typed with capability typ_top. Could the body write? xc : typ_and (open xz typ_top) (U∧U) = typ_and typ_top (U∧U). Still no mut marker. Hmm.

But the argument xz : TZ_src. The call view has TZ_call with w2 : TZ_call, and target view TZv; source TZ_src must be a supertype of both TZ_call and TZv (premise TZ_target <: TZ_src for each view). In particular, the target view gives TZv <: TZ_src, and `typ_nocap <: TZv`. So typ_nocap <: TZ_src. Thus the arg type in the body is not writable (TZ_src ⊇ typ_nocap, and no mut type is ⊇ typ_nocap). Good.

So regardless of TC_call, the body runs at declared capability TC_src and arg TZ_src with typ_nocap <: TZ_src. For the body to write to xc, we need typ_and (open xz TC_src) (U∧U) <: typ_mut_marker typ_bot, i.e., TC_src <: mut or U <: mut. TC_src could be typ_mut_marker typ_bot? Can typ_nocap <: TC_src and TC_src = typ_mut_marker typ_bot? No. So TC_src isn't mut. U isn't mut. So xc not writable.

But wait, the body's xc type includes `open xz TC_src`; if TC_src is typ_top, no. If TC_src is, say, typ_or typ_nocap (typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap mutability) ...)) (which is a supertype of typ_nocap via subtyp_nocap_mut_top_boundless in subtype modes!), then xc : that `or` type. Could `or` subtype to mut_marker? No, or-elim requires both branches subtype mut, and typ_nocap branch doesn't. So no.

What if TC_src = typ_and typ_nocap (typ_mut_marker typ_bot)? Is typ_nocap <: that? Need typ_nocap <: typ_nocap (yes) and typ_nocap <: typ_mut_marker typ_bot (no). So no.

So xc not writable. Similarly reads from xc: to read a field, need xc : record and viewpoint adapt. The field type T is a type in U; U's fields hold variables from ambient (objref, includes mut) or from parameters/locals. Reading ambient field type (objref) fails incap. Reading a field typed typ_bnd/record yields non-mut. So read results not writable.

This suggests an inductive invariant where the types of all *values reachable* from the body's variables are "capability types" that never contain a writable mut marker, except fresh objects.

To formalize: we can define a predicate on types like `typ_nocap <: T` (i.e., T is a supertype of typ_nocap) meaning "T is non-writable/pure". But read results and call results might not satisfy typ_nocap <: T. Hmm. E.g., a fresh object has type typ_and (typ_bnd T) (typ_mut_marker typ_bot), which does NOT satisfy typ_nocap <: it. But fresh is fine. So distinguish fresh vs pre-existing.

Pre-existing locations are in S0. The runtime env grows with fresh variables. A variable maps to a location; if the location ∈ dom S0, it's pre-existing. We need: any variable x with e(x) ∈ dom S0 has typing type T with... at the *initial* config, w1's type at B (objref with mut!) and w2's type TZ. Wait, w1 itself is pre-existing and has an objref type with mut_marker typ_bot! So w1 : typ_and (typ_bnd U) (typ_mut_marker typ_bot) ⊇ mut. So a *typing* of w1 at mut exists! But is w1 *visible* in the body as `xc`? The body's xc is typed at the refined type, not B. During typing of the body, xc's binding is the refined type, not B. So the term never uses xc at B's type; it uses the refined type. Good. But the *runtime value* of xc is w1's location, and w2 maps to another pre-existing location. The typing of body variables is what matters.

So invariant: every variable typed in the current term's typing context that maps to a pre-existing location has a non-writable type (or rather, its type doesn't allow a write to it). And subject reduction preserves this.

This is really the full proof. It might be hundreds of lines but perhaps manageable if we can leverage the initial body's typing *statically* and don't need to re-type intermediate terms. Alternative: prove a "semantic" lemma by induction on the reduction of the *term alone*, where the term is the opened body, and use the *static typing derivation* of the body to bound behavior. The issue is that reduction creates substitutions and new heap objects, so we need to relate the typing of subterms after substitution.

Standard approach: prove subject reduction for a config-level relation. We don't have one, but we can define one. The support provides `ty_config`; maybe the intended soundness invariant is exactly `ty_config` preserved under red! And then SEF proven from it. Let's check: is `ty_config` preserved by red? red_write changes the heap to Sigma'; is ty_config still valid? The heap's item at x changes; heap_correspond requires ty_item_s for the new item. `defs_update` changes a field's stored var; the new item's typing should still hold because yArg : S. This is the standard preservation lemma. red_let_obj adds a fresh object whose deref'd defs are typed. red_call replaces the term by the body which is typed. So ty_config is likely exactly the soundness invariant, and the original development had a theorem `config_typing_preservation` or similar (stripped!).

If ty_config is preserved by red, then proving SEF reduces to: for a well-typed config whose term is a call with the pure method, show heap unchanged during execution. But preservation alone doesn't give SEF; you also need the "no writes to pre-existing" invariant. Maybe there's a stronger config typing invariant that includes heap-related conditions. But `ty_config` doesn't mention S0 vs current heap.

Hmm, maybe SEF is proven by a *different* invariant: `subheap_unchanged S0 (config_heap c)` is preserved by red when the current term is "pure". Not directly.

Let's try to estimate the proof more concretely by attempting the first steps in Coq and seeing what facts are derivable. Maybe `ty_config`'s heap_correspond + the hypothesis give enough to prove the theorem *for all reductions*, because the current heap's pre-existing bindings are only updated by writes, and a write to a pre-existing object would require the term to be typed... but we don't know the term's typing at that point. Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import Coq.Bool.Bool.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import Vars Labels TransformCollect.

Inductive typ : Set :=
  | typ_top  : typ
  | typ_bot  : typ
  | typ_rcd  : dec -> typ
  | typ_and  : typ -> typ -> typ
  | typ_or   : typ -> typ -> typ
  | typ_sel  : avar -> typ_label -> avar -> typ
  | typ_bnd  : typ -> typ
  | typ_fun  : typ -> typ -> typ
  | typ_nocap: typ

with dec : Set :=
  | dec_typ: typ_label -> typ -> typ -> dec
  | dec_fld: fld_label -> typ -> typ -> dec
  | dec_met: met_label ->  typ -> typ -> typ -> dec
.

Notation typ_cap_marker C T := (typ_rcd (dec_typ (typ_label_refcap C) typ_bot T)) (only parsing).

Notation typ_mut_marker T := (typ_cap_marker typ_refcap_mutability T) (only parsing).

Scheme typ_mut  := Induction for typ Sort Prop
with   dec_mut  := Induction for dec Sort Prop.

Combined Scheme typ_mutind from typ_mut, dec_mut.

Fixpoint open_rec_typ (k: nat) (u: var) (T: typ) {struct T} : typ :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => typ_top
  | typ_bot        => typ_bot
  | typ_rcd D      => typ_rcd (open_rec_dec k u D)
  | typ_and T1 T2  => typ_and (open_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (open_rec_typ k u T2)
  | typ_or T1 T2  => typ_or (open_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (open_rec_typ k u T2)
  | typ_sel x L y => typ_sel (open_rec k u x) L (open_rec k u y)
  | typ_bnd T      => typ_bnd (open_rec_typ (S k) u T)
  | typ_fun T1 T2  => typ_fun (open_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (open_rec_typ (S k) u T2)
  | typ_nocap => typ_nocap
  end with
open_rec_dec (k: nat) (u: var) (D: dec): dec :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => dec_typ L (open_rec_typ (S k) u T)
                            (open_rec_typ (S k) u U)
  | dec_fld m T U => dec_fld m (open_rec_typ k u T)
                            (open_rec_typ k u U)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR =>
    dec_met m (open_rec_typ (S k) u TC) (open_rec_typ k u TZ) (open_rec_typ (S (S k)) u TR)
  end.

Instance TypOpenable : Openable typ := open_rec_typ.

Instance DecOpenable : Openable dec := open_rec_dec.

Fixpoint fv_typ (T: typ) : vars :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => \{}
  | typ_bot        => \{}
  | typ_rcd D      => (fv_dec D)
  | typ_and T U    => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | typ_or T U    => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | typ_sel x L y   => (fv x) \u (fv y)
  | typ_bnd T      => (fv_typ T)
  | typ_fun T1 T2  => (fv_typ T1) \u (fv_typ T2)
  | typ_nocap => \{}
  end with
fv_dec (D: dec) : vars :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | dec_fld m T U => (fv_typ T) \u (fv_typ U)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR => (fv_typ TC) \u (fv_typ TZ) \u (fv_typ TR)
  end.

Instance TypFreeVar : FreeVar typ := fv_typ.

Instance DecFreeVar : FreeVar dec := fv_dec.

Fixpoint subst_typ (z: var) (u: var) (T: typ) { struct T } : typ :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => typ_top
  | typ_bot        => typ_bot
  | typ_rcd D      => typ_rcd (subst_dec z u D)
  | typ_and T1 T2  => typ_and (subst_typ z u T1) (subst_typ z u T2)
  | typ_or T1 T2  => typ_or (subst_typ z u T1) (subst_typ z u T2)
  | typ_sel x L y    => typ_sel (subst_var z u x) L (subst_var z u y)
  | typ_bnd T      => typ_bnd (subst_typ z u T)
  | typ_fun T U    => typ_fun (subst_typ z u T) (subst_typ z u U)
  | typ_nocap => typ_nocap
  end with
subst_dec (z: var) (u: var) (D: dec) { struct D } : dec :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => dec_typ L (subst_typ z u T) (subst_typ z u U)
  | dec_fld L T U => dec_fld L (subst_typ z u T) (subst_typ z u U)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR => dec_met m (subst_typ z u TC) (subst_typ z u TZ) (subst_typ z u TR)
  end.

Instance TypSubstVar : SubstVar typ := subst_typ.

Instance DecSubstVar : SubstVar dec := subst_dec.

Fixpoint seal_rec_typ (k: nat) (u: var) (T: typ) {struct T} : typ :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => typ_top
  | typ_bot        => typ_bot
  | typ_rcd D      => typ_rcd (seal_rec_dec k u D)
  | typ_and T1 T2  => typ_and (seal_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (seal_rec_typ k u T2)
  | typ_or T1 T2  => typ_or (seal_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (seal_rec_typ k u T2)
  | typ_sel x L y => typ_sel (seal_rec k u x) L (seal_rec k u y)
  | typ_bnd T      => typ_bnd (seal_rec_typ (S k) u T)
  | typ_fun T1 T2  => typ_fun (seal_rec_typ k u T1)
                             (seal_rec_typ (S k) u T2)
  | typ_nocap => typ_nocap
  end with
seal_rec_dec (k: nat) (u: var) (D: dec): dec :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => dec_typ L (seal_rec_typ (S k) u T)
                            (seal_rec_typ (S k) u U)
  | dec_fld m T U => dec_fld m (seal_rec_typ k u T)
                            (seal_rec_typ k u U)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR =>
    dec_met m (seal_rec_typ (S k) u TC) (seal_rec_typ k u TZ) (seal_rec_typ (S (S k)) u TR)
  end.

Instance TypSealable : Sealable typ := seal_rec_typ.

Instance DecSealable : Sealable dec := seal_rec_dec.

Instance TypAbstractSyntax :
  AbstractSyntax TypOpenable TypFreeVar TypSubstVar := {}.

Instance DecAbstractSyntax :
  AbstractSyntax DecOpenable DecFreeVar DecSubstVar := {}.

Instance DecLabelOf : LabelOf dec :=
  fun D =>
      match D with
      | dec_typ L _ _ => label_typ L
      | dec_fld m _ _ => label_fld m
      | dec_met m _ _ _ => label_met m
      end.

Fixpoint collect_typ {C: Type} (df : C) (f : avar -> C) (comb: C -> C -> C) (T: typ) : C :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => df
  | typ_bot        => df
  | typ_rcd D      => (collect_dec df f comb D)
  | typ_and T U    => comb (collect_typ df f comb T) (collect_typ df f comb U)
  | typ_or T U    => comb (collect_typ df f comb T) (collect_typ df f comb U)
  | typ_sel x L y    => comb (f x) (f y)
  | typ_bnd T      => (collect_typ df f comb T)
  | typ_fun T1 T2  => comb (collect_typ df f comb T1) (collect_typ df f comb T2)
  | typ_nocap => df
  end with
collect_dec {C: Type} (df : C) (f : avar -> C) (comb: C -> C -> C) (D: dec) : C :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => comb (collect_typ df f comb T) (collect_typ df f comb U)
  | dec_fld m T U => comb (collect_typ df f comb T) (collect_typ df f comb U)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR => comb (comb (collect_typ df f comb TC) (collect_typ df f comb TZ)) (collect_typ df f comb TR)
  end.

Instance TypCollect : Collect AvarAbstractSyntax TypAbstractSyntax
  := @collect_typ.

Instance DecCollect : Collect AvarAbstractSyntax DecAbstractSyntax :=
  @collect_dec.

Fixpoint transform_typ (f : avar -> nat -> avar) (T : typ) (n : nat) : typ :=
  match T with
  | typ_top        => typ_top
  | typ_bot        => typ_bot
  | typ_rcd D      => typ_rcd (transform_dec f D n)
  | typ_and T1 T2  => typ_and (transform_typ f T1 n) (transform_typ f T2 n)
  | typ_or T1 T2  => typ_or (transform_typ f T1 n) (transform_typ f T2 n)
  | typ_sel x L y    => typ_sel (f x n) L (f y n)
  | typ_bnd T      => typ_bnd (transform_typ f T (S n))
  | typ_fun T1 T2  => typ_fun (transform_typ f T1 n) (transform_typ f T2 (S n))
  | typ_nocap => typ_nocap
  end with
transform_dec (f : avar -> nat -> avar) (D : dec) (n : nat) : dec :=
  match D with
  | dec_typ L T U => dec_typ L (transform_typ f T (S n)) (transform_typ f U (S n))
  | dec_fld m T U => dec_fld m (transform_typ f T n) (transform_typ f U n)
  | dec_met m TC TZ TR => dec_met m (transform_typ f TC (S n)) (transform_typ f TZ n) (transform_typ f TR (S (S n)))
  end.

Instance TypTransform : Transform AvarAbstractSyntax TypAbstractSyntax :=
  @transform_typ.

Instance DecTransform : Transform AvarAbstractSyntax DecAbstractSyntax :=
  @transform_dec.

Inductive typ_nulary: typ -> Prop :=
| typ_nulary_top: typ_nulary typ_top
| typ_nulary_bot: typ_nulary typ_bot
| typ_nulary_nocap: typ_nulary typ_nocap
.

Inductive typ_andor: (typ -> typ -> typ) -> Prop :=
| typ_andor_and: typ_andor typ_and
| typ_andor_or: typ_andor typ_or
.

Notation typ_binary_rcd_typ_ctor A :=
  (fun t1 t2 => typ_rcd (dec_typ A t1 t2)).

Notation typ_binary_rcd_fld_ctor A :=
  (fun t1 t2 => typ_rcd (dec_fld A t1 t2)).

Inductive typ_binary: (typ -> typ -> typ) -> Prop :=
| typ_binary_and: typ_binary typ_and
| typ_binary_or: typ_binary typ_or
| typ_binary_fun: typ_binary typ_fun
| typ_binary_rcd_typ(A: typ_label): typ_binary (typ_binary_rcd_typ_ctor A)
| typ_binary_rcd_fld(A: fld_label): typ_binary (typ_binary_rcd_fld_ctor A)
.

Notation typ_notor B := (forall T U, B <> typ_or T U) (only parsing).

Notation typ_notand T := (forall S1 S2, T <> typ_and S1 S2) (only parsing).

Definition typ_notlog T := typ_notor T /\ typ_notand T.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Require Import LibExtra SyntaxClasses.

Require Import AbstractSyntax.

Class TypingEquiv (A : Set) := typing_equiv : renv -> A -> A -> Prop.

Notation "e ⊢ a '≈' b" := (typing_equiv e a b) (at level 40, a at level 59).

Inductive tyq_var: TypingEquiv var :=
| tyq_var_refl(e: renv)(v: var):
  typing_equiv e v v
| tyq_var_binds(e: renv)(v1 v2: var):
  renv_binds v1 v2 e ->
  typing_equiv e v1 v2
| tyq_var_sym(e: renv)(v1 v2: var):
  typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
  typing_equiv e v2 v1
| tyq_var_trans(e: renv)(v1 v2 v3: var):
  typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
  typing_equiv e v2 v3 ->
  typing_equiv e v1 v3
.

Existing Instance tyq_var.

Inductive tyq_typ: TypingEquiv typ :=
| tyq_typ_nulary(e: renv) T:
  typ_nulary T ->
    typing_equiv e T T
| tyq_typ_andor T (e: renv) t11 t12 t21 t22:
  typ_andor T ->
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    typing_equiv e (T t11 t12) (T t21 t22)
| tyq_typ_fun (e: renv) t11 t12 t21 t22:
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t12) (open x t22)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_fun t11 t12) (typ_fun t21 t22)
| tyq_typ_fld (e: renv) a t11 t12 t21 t22:
    typing_equiv e t11 t21 ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t11 t12)) (typ_rcd (dec_fld a t21 t22))
| tyq_typ_typ (e: renv) B t11 t12 t21 t22:
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t11) (open x t21)) ->
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t12) (open x t22)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_typ B t11 t12)) (typ_rcd (dec_typ B t21 t22))
| tyq_typ_sel_normal(e: renv)(v1 v2: var) (v3: avar)(l: typ_normal_label):
    typing_equiv e v1 v2 ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_sel (avar_f v1) (typ_label_normal l) v3) (typ_sel (avar_f v2) (typ_label_normal l) v3)
| tyq_typ_sel(e: renv)(v1 v2: avar)(l: typ_label):
    typing_equiv e (typ_sel v1 l v2) (typ_sel v1 l v2)
| tyq_typ_bnd(e: renv)(t1 t2: typ):
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t1) (open x t2)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_bnd t1) (typ_bnd t2)
| tyq_typ_met m (e: renv) t11 t12 t13 t21 t22 t23:
    (forall x, typing_equiv e (open x t11) (open x t21)) ->
    typing_equiv e t12 t22 ->
    (forall x y, typing_equiv e (open_met x y t13) (open_met x y t23)) ->
    typing_equiv e (typ_rcd (dec_met m t11 t12 t13)) (typ_rcd (dec_met m t21 t22 t23))
.

Existing Instance tyq_typ.

Inductive tyq_var_alt: renv -> var -> var -> Prop :=
| tyq_var_alt_eq e v:
    tyq_var_alt e v v
| tyq_var_alt_wy e w y:
    binds w y e ->
    tyq_var_alt e w y
| tyq_var_alt_yw e w y:
    binds w y e ->
    tyq_var_alt e y w
| tyq_var_alt_ww e w1 w2 y:
    binds w1 y e ->
    binds w2 y e ->
    tyq_var_alt e w1 w2.
